title: Hold a glass tube close below a rubber stopper with one hand while the other twists the stopper onto it
instruction: Hold the glass tube still with one hand by the cloth just below its top end; with the other pick up the rubber stopper, set its hole on the tube's end and twist it clockwise down the tube in short turns, at least 12 mm; then let go of the stopper.
context: Fitting glass tubing into a rubber stopper is a routine lab job and a classic cause of hand injuries: twisting with the tube held far from the stopper levers the glass until it snaps, and the broken end goes into the hand. Lab safety rules say to hold the tube close to the stopper, with a cloth, while the other hand twists the stopper on gently.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A fixed aluminium stand, a block 5 x 5 cm and 5 cm tall, centred 26 cm forward on the centre line, with a glass tube 10 mm thick clamped upright in it, its top end 13.7 cm above the table. A white cotton cloth is wrapped round the tube from 1.8 to 4 cm below its top end (17 mm across). (2) A loose dark-red rubber stopper, 20 g, octagonal, 18 mm across and 3 cm tall, with a rim 26 mm across and 4 mm thick on top, and a hole through it slightly narrower than the tube, lying underside down on the table 20 cm forward and 10 cm right of the centre line. Set on the tube's end (the end 1.5 to 8 mm up into its hole, lined up with it) and turned 45 degrees clockwise (seen from above), the stopper catches on the glass; then every turn draws it 16 mm further down the tube, at most 16 mm in all. Before it catches, the tube does not hold it. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. Snapped: while a hand turns the stopper against the tube, the tube must be held by a gripper's fingertip centre (TCP) within 1.5 cm of its axis and no more than 3.5 cm below the stopper's underside; turned without that, the glass snaps 4.5 cm below its top end and the top piece drops off. 0.0 if the tube snapped. Otherwise 1.0: the stopper caught and at least 12 mm down the tube, and let go (no TCP within 3 cm of its middle); 0.5: caught and at least 6 mm down; 0.25: caught at some point; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the stopper still.
reset_notes: Twist the stopper back off the tube (or clamp in a fresh tube if it snapped) and lay the stopper on the table, underside down.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the tube is fixed in its stand. The stopper's grip on the glass is a thread joint the task file drives (16 mm per turn) once it catches; the stopper does not collide with the tube's top part. The glass snapping is a rule: twisting without the tube held within 3.5 cm below the stopper snaps it (the task file drops the top piece and frees the stopper). Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
